summary: All five orders filled. The three sells executed ahead of the two buys, so the Implicator's sequencing risk never arose and Staples ended at about 13.9% by bucket (WMT 8.05%, KR 5.88%), down from 15.5%. Health Care is about 12.9% (IDXX 8.06%, INCY 2.44%, EXEL 2.38%), and the INCY+EXEL oncology pair is about 4.8%, inside the limit I set. Equity closed at $628.31 (+$3.09). The SPY benchmark fell about 0.36% on the day. Since version 6 started on 11-10, the agent is +0.93%, against +0.59% for SPY and -0.45% for the shadow. That is a few sessions and not evidence about today's choices. Judged on the information available, the sells hold up. VNQ's stored clause had tripped. The WMT trim answered a company-confirmed print 4 sessions out on the largest single stock. IEF went under L8 with its stop 0.8% away. The two buys have three weak points. (1) I accepted EXEL's $65 stop as '9.4% under the $71.74 menu close'. The fill came at $69.04, so the stop is only about 5.8% under the fill (stop block: 6.15% above the $69.00 mark). That is tighter than the 8-10% I use for other single stocks, and the stored text measures from a price we never paid. The Skeptic flagged exactly this, and I let it through unfixed, which repeats an L6 miss. (2) KR's stored invalidation measures $61.50 from 'the $69.81 mark on 11-13' and from the original lot. The figure that matters is the blended cost, now about $67.06, and $61.50 sits about 8.3% under it. The level is fine; the wording breaks L6. (3) On a risk-off call, the swap sold low-beta sleeves (VNQ 0.325, IEF 0.103, part of WMT) and bought EXEL (0.628). On reported betas, stress improves slightly because of KR's negative beta. If KR's beta is treated as zero, as its own thesis says it should be, the book's 10% stress loss is slightly worse than before. The amounts are small, but my reasoning didn't say so. Cash is about $86 (13.7% of equity) against the shadow's 99.5% invested. I justified that with Nvidia on 11-17 and WMT on 11-19 and committed to deploy after those prints. The next runs should keep that commitment and not let the reason go stale. Holdings at the close: no price stop tripped. BND is the only stop alert (NEAR, +0.8% above $70), and it is already named the next sell candidate. VOO and VTI are 3.48% above the SPY 200-day stop going into the Nvidia print. Qualitative clauses: no 8-K, guidance cut or confirmed KR cyber link appeared in today's notes.
lessons: L6 for new buys: a stop set before the fill has to be measured from a menu close or mark. At the first run after the fill, restate the distance from the actual fill through thesis_updates. EXEL is due tomorrow: the $65 stop is about 5.8% under the $69.04 fill, not 9.4%. Either store that honestly or move it to about $62.50 (about 9.5% under the fill) to match the other single stocks. Pick one and explain the choice.

When an add creates a blended position, measure the stop from the blended average cost, not from the day's mark or the oldest lot. KR's $61.50 is about 8.3% under the roughly $67.06 blended cost. Restate KR's invalidation text to say that and drop 'the $69.81 mark on 11-13'.
When I accept a Skeptic 'data' objection about stop wording, fix the wording in the same decision. Leaving it 'to restate later' has now caused an L6 miss twice (INCY 11-11, EXEL and KR 11-13).

On a risk-off day, state the net change in book beta from a rotation, using the stress figure with KR's artifact beta set to zero. Don't rely on the Implicator's headline stress number, which KR's -0.61 beta flatters.

Idle cash commitment: cash is 13.7%, about $23 above the 10% buffer. The 11-13 reason (Nvidia 11-17, WMT 11-19) expires after 11-19. From 11-20, cash above the buffer should go to Health Care or Staples proposals, or the decision should give a new, specific reason. If BND's stop trips first, cash rises toward 20%, which makes this more pressing.
WMT trim test: grade it on the stored SPY-relative wording over the 5 sessions after the 11-19 print. Today's +1.2% close above the $127.58 fill is one day and not evidence.
